name: smith

attributes.attribute: worked metal into useful and ornamented objects
the smith god of the Irish tales

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The smith is a figure of Irish and continental Celtic myth. From the start of the culture, the working of metal was one of the chief sources of its wealth. The smith melted the ore of iron and of gold and shaped it into the useful and the ornamented. The land held the smith in high regard. In the tales, the smith carried the power of magic and of the alchemist. The Irish god Goibniu and the Welsh Govannon both stand for this craft. The story links the smith with the magical cow of the bounty, the Glas Ghaibhleann. So the smith, the maker of the tool, stands near the wealth of the land. The folk honored the smoke, the forge, and the hand that turned the ore into the blade and the ring.
